# GEO report: trailhead

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 50–59/100, Needs work

Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 11.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 50. High = (11.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 59.

The site has four real problems. Pages are built in the browser only. The Trail guides page is marked `noindex`. The sitemap line in `robots.txt` is not an absolute URL. The only link to the guides page is a button. One rule (canonical links) can't be settled from code because no domain is declared. No blocker cap applies, because the home page is not noindex.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Render the pages on the server (GEO-003)
- **Why it matters:** many crawlers read only the HTML the server first sends and don't run JavaScript. With browser-only rendering they may see an empty page.
- **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2`
- **What the code says:** `ssr: false,`
- **Size:** Medium. Remove the setting, or prerender the routes.
- **Score after this:** 63–72

### 2. Make the `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt an absolute URL (GEO-011)
- **Why it matters:** crawlers expect a full address, so the relative path may not lead them to your sitemap.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4`
- **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml`
- **Size:** Small. Change it to `https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml`, or whatever your real domain is.
- **Score after this:** 59–67

### 3. Link to the guides page with a real link (GEO-016)
- **Why it matters:** crawlers find pages by following `<a href>` links. The only route to `/guides` is a script-driven button.
- **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8`
- **What the code says:** `<button @click="router.push('/guides')">Trail guides</button>`
- **Size:** Small. Use `<NuxtLink to="/guides">`.
- **Score after this:** 59–67

Another problem sits just below the top three (1.5 points lost). `/guides` is listed in your sitemap but sends `noindex`, which tells search engines to ignore it:
- `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` has `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');`.
- Remove that rule, or take `/guides` out of the sitemap.
- Fixing it alone moves the score to about 56–64.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`; plain text, valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers are allowed as policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2`; only `/admin` is blocked. I assumed you want to be found. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`; `/guides` is noindex, `/` is fine (1 of 2 routes clear) |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on the declared origin | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical tag anywhere, and no declared origin |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:2`; site-wide |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD in the code |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4`; relative Sitemap line. `public/sitemap.xml` is valid. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Problem | Not run | `app.vue:2`; `/` is clear, `/guides` has no title or description of its own and uses the shared default (1 of 2 routes clear). `lang="en"` is set at `nuxt.config.ts:5`. |
| GEO-016 | Routes reachable through plain links | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8`; `/guides` is reachable only by a button (0 of 1 routes clear) |
| GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` in `headers.ts` or the page metadata |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read `app.vue` and the three pages. They have no images, and the button has text. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No mobile app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` present. That's fine. |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app project |

## Can't tell from code

- **GEO-015 (canonical):** no canonical link exists and there is no `geo.config.json` declaring your domain. The sitemap uses `trailhead.example`, which looks like a placeholder. Tell me your real domain and I can treat this rule as a plain missing-canonical problem. If you add one canonical per page, the score could reach up to 59 on this rule alone.
- **Hosting of `headers.ts`:** the middleware only runs if the site is served by a Nitro server. A fully static deploy wouldn't send that header, so confirm with a live check.
- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. If you have an access log, `geopilot logs <access log>` checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Listed URLs:** whether `https://trailhead.example/` and `/guides` really answer 200 is a live-only check.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site.
- I treated `/admin` as intentionally hidden. It is both disallowed in `robots.txt` and `noindex`, and it isn't in the sitemap or linked, so I didn't count it. Because crawlers can't fetch a disallowed page, the `noindex` there is never seen. That's harmless here.
- I sampled all three routes (`/`, `/guides`, `/admin`).
- Blocking training crawlers such as `GPTBot` is a separate choice from search access. Nothing blocks them here.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
